title.narrative: Elnino Flood Response in Samburu operational Grant

description.narrative: The Kenya Meteolological department predicted El Nino rains to come from mid October. The, rains started at the end of October and caused heavy flooding that reached a peak on the 2nd of November. Samburu County is one of the worst effected regions in Kenya, and has been selected as we have a strong presence through local partners that will enable a timely response. In Samburu County, the most affected areas are Samburu East and North sub-counties. Phone discussions with local community leaders has provided a total of 9023 people having been affected at the villages of Lerata, Tangar, Noit, Anderi, Naisunyai and Laparaan . A spike in rainfall is projected due to the ongoing El Nino rains and Samburu county may become affected with a further population of 9366 people being displaced in other locations that have not be badly hit at the moment. No major support has reached the community except the rescue missions by the helicopter from the Ormalo Ranch that rescued 8 people that had been swept away in their vehicle. The funding from Caritas Australia in addition to CAFOD funding(CGF &GEF) will come in handy in adressing the immediate needs of affected population of 6,076 people in the worst affected villages of Anderi, Laparan, Noit and Tangar in Samburu North and Lerata and Naisunyai in Samburu East, supporting them with food, NFIs, and water treatment chemicals. This is a 45day project implementation following Start Model with a reporting period of one month
